implementationCovered: Read-only A2A service cards are discoverable at /.well-known/agent-card.json and /.well-known/seller-agent-card.json; their descriptions explicitly state they are not CIS-8004 identity attestations.
Buyer records and fsyncs a hash-linked transaction dispatch intent with reviewed parties and amount before sending the signed seller request. It stores no raw signed payload or private key.
Local JSONL audit rejects files above 16 MiB and refuses an append that would cross the configured bound.
A2A JSON-RPC endpoint supports browser preflight for POST and protocol headers while exposing only read-only actions.
limits: A dispatch intent proves neither that a request reached the seller nor that a transaction settled; operators must reconcile the hash and must not retry blindly.
Audit storage remains a local single-writer JSONL file on the configured disk. There is no shared transactional store, retention automation, multi-instance locking, or external tamper anchor.

A2A discovery tests use the project's own SDK server and fixture actions. No independently implemented third-party or pre-existing agent was run, so this does not establish hackathon eligibility or a user pilot.
No fresh Registry read, payment, production deployment, public endpoint check, or mainnet test was performed.
